messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: P1 - Paging surge detected on serving-cluster-us-west-2. Elevated OOMs during model init. Auto-mitigation triggered: reduce-concurrency policy applied to pool-42. Thread opened 1719987654
lee: Ack. I'm looking at the load graphs now. :eyes:
josh: seeing repeated "OOM: failed to allocate GPU memory" in warmup logs for model Llama-34B-q8 on node gpu-17. Also lots of "failed to deserialize shard: checksum mismatch" entries.
maya: Summary from metrics: model-inits spiked at 03:12 UTC -> ~120 concurrent attempts. Page cache thrash + RAM/GPU pressure. Paging writes increased 4x.
lee: Is this hitting customer-facing endpoints or just background warmups?
mei: Support trend: org "BrightArc" reporting 502s starting 03:14. Telemetry shows increased tail latency on /v1/generate.
ryan: Can we confirm if compile timeouts are present too? Last week saw compile-timeouts under high parallelism.
josh: Yes — interleaved compile timeouts then deserialize errors. Excerpt:
[2026-03-12T03:13:02Z] WARN kernel-loader: compile shard 3 timeout=10000ms
[2026-03-12T03:13:03Z] ERROR deser: checksum mismatch shard=2 expected=0x9fa3 got=0x0
[2026-03-12T03:13:04Z] FATAL gpu-allocator: OOM allocate 3.2G
ana: rolling back warmup autoscaler? Auto-mitigation reduced concurrency but queued init attempts still in flight.
maya: Immediate mitigations proposed:
- throttle new routing to affected pool (partial applied)
- evict Llama-34B-q8 from nodes with highest page-in rates
- enable fallback routing to lighter model Llama-7B-quant for BrightArc
- pause background model prefetching for 10m
lee: Running evict on worst node and enabling fallback now.
lee: ```sh
# evict model from node
curl -XPOST "https://infra-api.internal/nodes/gpu-17/evict" -d '{"model":"Llama-34B-q8"}'
```
incident-bot: JOB queued: evict job id evict-4821 created; ETA 30s
josh: After evict, run kvcache flush to free RAM: `adminctl kvcache flush --node gpu-17`.
lee: Evict job completed. Node shows drop in page-ins and GPU alloc failures stopped for that node.
mei: BrightArc 502s reduced from ~12% -> ~1.2% over last 5m. They confirm degraded but usable.
ryan: Next: prevent stampede on model load. Propose token-bucket limiter on model-init and singleflight loader per model id.
josh: Deploying hotfix to runtime: gate concurrent init with singleflight + exponential backoff on deser. Rolling to canary (3 nodes).
maya: Canary looks good; compile times normal. Propose short-term per-account parallel-init quota = 2 for 30m.
lee: Implementing account quota via routing rules.
nana: Notifying next on-call: @ryan will take handoff at 04:00 UTC.
ryan: I'll be on. ETA to remove risk ~45m after rollout. Drafting customer note for BrightArc.
mei: Draft comms:
"We experienced resource pressure causing elevated failures between 03:12-03:40 UTC. Root cause: concurrent model warmups triggering GPU/RAM paging and deserialization errors. Mitigation: throttled warmups, evicted heavy instances, routed traffic to a lower-capacity model. Service returned to normal for most customers."
lee: Adding incident tags: root_cause=concurrent_warmup_stampede impact=partial_customer_errors mitigations=evict/throttle/fallback
josh: Postmortem actions:
- enforce singleflight model loads
- add checksum-on-fetch + re-fetch on mismatch
- limit simultaneous inits per node
- improve warmup circuit breaker with backoff
- add alert for checksum-mismatch spike
maya: Runbook updated and SRE task created to adjust autoscaler smoothing to avoid aggressive prefetch.
nana: Handoff: I'm handing off to @ryan in 10m. Status: mitigations applied, hotfix rolling 3/3 canary then prod.
ryan: Taking over. Monitor channels; escalate if 502s >2% for any customer or OOMs reappear. If regress, revert hotfix and re-enable evicted model later.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded P1 -> P2 at 1719987900 after customer impact reduced. Timeline and actions logged.
lee: thanks team. Logging notes and will start draft postmortem.
